business_rules: Inputs are the principal (up to 9 digits plus 2 decimals), the annual rate as a percentage (up to 3 digits plus 3 decimals), the number of compounding periods per year (0 to 99) and the number of years (0 to 99).
The number of periods is compounds per year multiplied by years.
When the number of periods is 0, nothing compounds and the maturity amount equals the principal.
Each period multiplies the running balance by (100 x periods per year + annual rate) divided by (100 x periods per year), which is 1 plus the annual rate per period.
The running balance is stored rounded half-up (COBOL ROUNDED) to the cent after every period, so rounding differences accumulate period by period exactly as in the legacy program.
Maturity amount is the running balance after the last period, in PIC 9(9)V99 (two decimals, no sign).
Accrued interest is maturity amount minus the original principal, rounded half-up, in a signed PIC S9(9)V99 field.
A balance that grows beyond nine integer digits loses its high-order digits, as in COBOL.

Inputs are the opening balance (signed), the day's total deposits, the day's total withdrawals, the overdraft threshold (signed, so it can be negative) and the overdraft fee, all in two-decimal amounts.
The day's balance is the opening balance plus deposits minus withdrawals.
If that balance is strictly below the overdraft threshold, the overdraft fee is applied and the overdraft flag is 1. A balance exactly equal to the threshold is not an overdraft.
Otherwise the fee applied is 0.00 and the overdraft flag is 0.
The closing balance is the day's balance minus the fee applied. It is signed and can go negative.
No ROUNDED clause is used anywhere: every store truncates toward zero (COBOL default). All amounts have two decimals, so no rounding actually occurs for valid inputs.
Fee applied is stored in PIC 9(5)V99 and the flag in PIC 9; the closing balance is stored in PIC S9(9)V99.

Inputs are the loan principal (up to 9 digits plus 2 decimals), the annual interest rate as a percentage (up to 3 digits plus 3 decimals, for example 3.333) and the term in whole months (up to 3 digits).
The monthly interest rate is the annual rate divided by 1200, that is annual percent divided by 12 months and by 100.
When the term is 0 months, the monthly payment is 0.00.
When the annual rate is 0, the monthly payment is the principal divided evenly by the number of months, rounded half-up to the cent.

Otherwise the monthly payment is the standard amortization payment: principal times the monthly rate, divided by 1 minus (1 + monthly rate) raised to the power of minus the term. The whole expression is evaluated at full precision and rounded half-up (COBOL ROUNDED) once, when stored.
Total payable is the already-rounded monthly payment multiplied by the term in months, rounded half-up to the cent.
Total interest is total payable minus the principal, rounded half-up to the cent. Because the rounded payment is used, total interest can differ by a few cents from an unrounded calculation.
All three results are stored in PIC 9(9)V99 fields: two decimal places, no sign, and nine integer digits. A value too large for the field loses its high-order digits, as it does on the mainframe.
